biography: Francisco "Cisco" Horta's journey began amidst the vibrant chaos of São Paulo's karting scene. Born into a family with modest means, Cisco's talent was undeniable from the start, hustling for every advantage against wealthier competitors. His raw speed caught the eye of a local Porsche team owner who gave him his first big break in the Porsche Carrera Cup Brasil. Cisco quickly became a fan favorite, not just for his pace but also for his flamboyant style, often celebrating overtakes with elaborate gestures. A near-fatal crash at Interlagos in 2018 forced him to re-evaluate his risk-taking, and while his outright aggression has mellowed slightly, the flash and flair remain, making him a seasoned veteran capable of surprising bursts of brilliance, even if consistency remains elusive. Now, as he approaches his late thirties, Cisco is regarded as a veteran presence, offering guidance to younger drivers while still chasing podiums in select Porsche-supported series.
drivingStyle: Horta's driving style is a blend of Brazilian flair and calculated aggression. He is known for his late-braking maneuvers and aggressive corner entries, often pushing the limits of grip to gain positions. Tire management has been a weakness in the past, but he's worked to improve his consistency. While not the most technically refined driver, Cisco thrives under pressure, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest, showcasing a remarkable ability to find that extra tenth of a second when it truly matters.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry from their karting days, fueled by contrasting personalities: Vargas, the calculating engineer, versus Horta, the instinctive showman.
A recent clash in the Porsche Carrera Cup Brasil, sparked by an aggressive overtake that resulted in Monteiro's retirement. Tensions remain high.
Horta and Rossi have battled for position on track numerous times, resulting in several on-track incidents and heated words in the media.

quirks: Always wears a lucky charm given to him by his grandmother - a small, worn wooden cross - tucked into his racing suit.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba song just before getting into the car to calm his nerves.
Insists on having a double espresso with exactly two sugars precisely 30 minutes before each race.
famousQuote: "Racing is not just about being the fastest; it's about making a statement. It's about leaving your mark on the track. And looking good while doing it, of course!"
careerHighlight: Winning the 2016 Porsche Carrera Cup Brasil championship after a season-long battle, securing the title with a dramatic last-lap overtake at Interlagos.
careerLowPoint: His horrific crash at Interlagos in 2018. The incident left him with serious injuries and forced him to miss half a season, prompting serious questions about his future in racing.
